text:
The Sabres' three-game winning streak ended at KeyBank Center, and it ended late. Buffalo led 1-0 on Peyton Krebs's deflected goal in the second period, then watched Ottawa score twice in the last nine minutes of the third: Shane Pinto on a backhand at 11:33, and Michael Amadio on a snap shot at 16:51 that held up as the winner. Amadio, the second star, was a 90th overall pick by the Kings in 2014 who worked through the AHL with Ontario before finding a place in the NHL.

The result matched the play. Our numbers give OTT 3.14 expected goals (a measure of the quality of chances) to BUF's 2.05, and by our simulation of every shot, Ottawa deserved to win 69 percent of the time. The Senators out-chanced Buffalo in all three periods, most clearly in the second, 1.10 to 0.56, even as they trailed on the scoreboard. They also won 37 of 53 faceoffs and put 30 shots on goal to Buffalo's 24. Neither power play converted, each team going 0 for 2.

The goaltending kept it close. Samuel Ersson, the first star, stopped 23 of 24, which was 1.05 goals better than the chances he faced would suggest. Ellis, the third star, saved 1.14 goals above expected on 30 shots, and without him this was a bigger gap. Tim Stützle's line drove much of the play, with Ottawa outchancing Buffalo 1.68 to 0.73 while he was on the ice. Buffalo's winning streak is over at three games, and Ottawa leaves with the win.
